match_note: There are three referees. R1 and R3 report in all three rounds; R2 reports only in round 1. The first-round manuscript differs from arXiv v1 in several ways. Referees quote the title 'Hidden Moiré Topology' and phrases such as 'hidden moiré in reciprocal space', 'translational commensurability is lost', 'new paradigm' and 'quantitatively reproduces'; none of these appear in v1, whose title is 'Resolving the Bulk-Boundary Correspondence Paradox...'. R3 describes Fig. S9(b) as a monoclinic (103) surface supercell; in v1, Fig. S9 is six-layer slab Fermi surfaces. R3 assigns Fig. 1(f) to the flat region and Fig. 1(e) to the disordered region, the reverse of v1. R3 cites Ref. 19 as Zheng et al. on TaAs; in v1, Ref. 19 is Trescher et al. The authors also mention Figs. S10/S11 as different surface terminations, which in v1 are bulk Fermi surface data. The core data, the LCM N=3 argument, the SFAL suggestion and the momentum-space moiré language are already in v1.

concerns.quote: they use the acronym SFAL at the bottom of page 6 before it is defined on page 7
concerns.summary: The acronym SFAL is used before it is defined.

concerns.quote: The authors need to explicitly justify why this should be classified as "Moiré" physics rather than standard "surface reconstruction" or "Umklapp folding."
concerns.summary: 'Moiré topology', 'hidden moiré' and 'new paradigm' overhype what is ordinary band folding on a high-index surface, with no competing interaction and no moiré flat bands.

concerns.quote: The authors cannot claim the framework "quantitatively reproduces" the spectra while simultaneously admitting it fails to capture the topological connectivity (loops vs. open arcs).
concerns.summary: The LCM-based calculation gives open arcs rather than the claimed closed Fermi-arc loops, so the authors should either compute the loops (e.g. with mixed terminations) or retreat from claims of full agreement.

concerns.quote: What is physically new about the LCM criterion beyond standard crystallographic projection arithmetic?
concerns.summary: The LCM criterion is standard commensurability arithmetic, equivalent to the real-space intercept method for constructing high-index surface cells, and is presented as a new discovery.

concerns.quote: it is possible that the "new smaller SBZ" is simply a result of a physical surface reconstruction (i.e., atoms moving to new equilibrium positions)
concerns.summary: The reduced surface Brillouin zone could come from a real structural surface reconstruction rather than interference of bulk projections.

concerns.quote: the DFT calculations assume a specific ideal termination (Si-Al). Did the authors perform structural relaxation in their DFT?
concerns.summary: The referee asks whether the DFT slabs were structurally relaxed and whether they reconstruct into a 3x1 supercell.

concerns.quote: can the authors rule out that the "closed loops" are not a result of surface magnetism or surface-induced magnetic ordering, rather than the LCM mechanism?
concerns.summary: The calculations use non-magnetic Nd, so the loop features might instead come from surface magnetism or spin fluctuations of the Nd moments.

concerns.quote: Thus, there is no inherent mismatch between the bulk and surface periodicities.
concerns.summary: Claims of inherent bulk-surface mismatch and lost commensurability are a misconception: with the proper (103) surface cell and a complete 3D-to-2D projection, the SBZ is perfectly commensurate.

concerns.quote: The proper (103) surface unit cell in Fig.S9(b) should be included in the main text Fig.1.
concerns.summary: Fig. 1(a) should show the proper multi-cell (103) surface unit cell instead of the single-cell zigzag depiction.

concerns.quote: The need of multiple bulk BZ projection to SBZ to fully account for the topological surface states is not uncommon.
concerns.summary: Multi-zone bulk projection is already known, e.g. for the CeX rock-salt (001) surface (Kuroda et al., PRL 2018).

concerns.quote: the low-symmetry/high-index surface of inversion-breaking Weyl semimetal such as TaAs have already been studied by Zheng et al in Ref.19
concerns.summary: Low-symmetry surfaces of Weyl semimetals have been studied before (TaAs), which limits the novelty.

later_concerns.quote: The abstract continues to suggest that the calculations quantitatively reproduce the observed spectra, even though the body of the paper now admits that... the loop-like connectivity, is not reproduced
later_concerns.summary: In round 2, the title and abstract still overstate theory-experiment agreement, which conflicts with the revised body text.

later_concerns.quote: the revised manuscript still retains much of the same expansive framing, including the title "Hidden Moiré Topology," references to a "new paradigm," and suggestions of flat-band engineering
later_concerns.summary: In round 2, overclaiming terms (hidden moiré, inherent mismatch, lost commensurability) were defended in the rebuttal but not changed in the manuscript.

later_concerns.quote: The reduced SBZ compared to bulk BZ is not from the so-called "hidden moire" but the results of normal practice in surface science and crystallography.
later_concerns.summary: In round 2, the referee says the proper surface cell and complete projection are default practice, and that the authors ignored the CeX/Kuroda example.

later_concerns.quote: The evidence for closed surface Fermi-arc loops remains suggestive rather than definitive.
later_concerns.summary: In round 3, the SFAL hybridization mechanism is seen as interpretation only, and the referee asks for cautious wording on 'closed loops' and 'generalized BBC' in the SI.

later_concerns.quote: it refers to the surface-state Fermi surface in Fig. 1e and the suppression of surface states in Fig. 1f, whereas the main text and Fig. 1 caption identify Fig. 1e as the uneven/disordered region
later_concerns.summary: In round 3, the SI's Fig. 1e/1f labels are inconsistent with the main text.

first_round.quote: I recommend the manuscript for publication in Nature Communications. The only change that needs to be made is that they use the acronym SFAL ... before it is defined

Before further consideration, I suggest that the authors provide a more rigorous reconciliation of the discrepancy between the theoretical model and the experimental results; and use a precise physical definition
the manuscript has many overclaims and even misconception, which make it unacceptable for the high standard of Nat. Comm. ... the current manuscript does not meet the high standard of Nat. Comm.

recommendations.note: First round is Version 0 in this file; nothing indicates a transfer from another journal. No referee co-signed another's report. R1 asked to publish with only an acronym fix, which maps to minor revision under the stated rule. R2 asked for substantial theoretical reconciliation or retreat from claims plus toned-down terminology, so major revision. R3 judged the paper unsuitable for the journal, so reject. R2 did not take part in later rounds. In later rounds R1 asked for further revision and then recommended publication after minor corrections; R3 kept rejecting in Version 1 and found it suitable for publication in Version 2.
recommendations.label: contested
